parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a documented, criminal, birth-sex facility rule reaching private businesses in the division with national passport and entry-screening exposure that can lead to refusal and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility. Detention, hormone withdrawal and documented custody abuse raise severity if arrested, while functioning courts, pending challenges, existing X passports remaining valid and no documented visitor enforcement under the new law prevent a severe-risk rating.

entry_documents.exposure: X passports no longer issued; existing X valid until expiry. Trans travellers report confiscation/blocking. Entry cable requires refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; civil-liberties suit challenges policy, though Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect. Limited fraud waivers exist.
entry_documents.interaction: Division X licence may diverge from passport available nationally, increasing mismatch at hotels, police checks and entry; visitor cannot obtain a matching national document.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Division bathroom offence carries up to one year jail. National corrections model removes hormones and imposes psychiatric treatment; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. A comparable arrest involved 24 hours in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division prisoners may receive hormone therapy under 2024 national ruling; courts released the comparable arrestee on pretrial release.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Bathroom arrest can progress to birth-sex custody, hormone denial and abuse, amplified by national corrections policy adopted from 2026.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law, effective 1 July 2026, criminalises restroom/changing-room use not matching birth sex in government and public-facing private businesses including restaurants, gas stations, entertainment and hospitals.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Litigation filed before effective date; a separate state statute has exemptions and requires refusal to depart, but that does not govern the division law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Everyday use of toilets in shops, transport and hospitals is a universal, unavoidable exposure; private businesses cannot offer an inclusive alternative.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors banned in 27 state/provinces; national orders restrict funding and proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18. Detention hormone removal documented.
care_services.protection: Several national orders have been blocked or enjoined; division prisoners retain hormone-therapy access under 2024 ruling.
care_services.interaction: Hospital bathroom criminalisation and ward practices can interrupt emergency care; travelling minor's care access depends on unsettled litigation.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order defines sex as binary at birth; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; schools investigations target pronoun use. Polls show majority support for birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts have enjoined several orders and hear challenges to passport and division laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases discretion and hostility, while courts provide partial but not currently effective relief for the facility rule.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division requires schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; teacher pronoun law; birth certificates cannot be changed. A 2022 felony travel-for-care bill was blocked and is not law.
minors_guardians.protection: Blocked felony bill, parental-permission routes in health board rules, and court challenges to national minor-care measures.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with a minor faces disclosure, school, healthcare and hospital-facility exposures; minor cannot use facilities matching identity without criminal risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific trans-violence rate materially above general homicide was identified. National bias incidents are reported, but dossier does not document organised police sweeps or extortion of visitors in this division.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law exists, though only 23 state/provinces cover gender identity in bias statutes; municipal gender-identity ordinances reach about 40% of division population.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of documented visitor violence is not evidence of safety; police are also directed nationally to investigate gender-ideology promotion in schools.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Suit outcome and a reported 16 June 2026 narrowing are not established as in force; offence classification disputed between misdemeanour and felony; no enforcement record under division measure identified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Pending due-process, equal-protection and privacy challenge could alter exposure; courts have enjoined other national measures.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty does not cancel the text of the criminal rule: traveller carries the possibility of arrest regardless of eventual litigation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal birth-sex facility exposure with rejected complaints, but this case is lower because the division rule is criminal, reaches private businesses, and carries up to one year jail, plus national entry-fraud risk.
Lower than 0.45-A: that anchor has facility exclusion by removal without documented criminalisation or border fraud exposure, whereas here arrest, custody and private-business reach apply.

Higher than 0.25-D: no documented police extortion, routine transport stops or hospital ward campaign in the division, and courts actively entertain challenges, though the core facility exposure remains tier-1.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is document or presentation mismatch leading to bathroom exclusion, trespass arrest, birth-sex custody and possible immigration fraud consequences. Private-business reach makes avoidance impractical, and national custody and hormone policies worsen detention. Courts, existing passport validity and absence of documented visitor enforcement under the new law are mitigations, but no remedy currently restores identity-congruent facilities. This places the regime near unremedied universal-exposure anchors, below organised-targeting profiles.
